    Run a GROBID service on multiple files (batch processing)

    grobid_process_files.Rd

    Applies grobid_process_file() to a vector of PDF files (or .txt for "processCitationList"), with sequential execution (with optional progress bar) or parallel execution.

    Unlike grobid_process_file(), this function does not accept a vector of raw text citations for "processCitationList": files must always be a vector of paths to existing files on disk. To directly process citations without an intermediate file, use grobid_process_file().

    Usage

    grobid_process_files(
  files,
  service = "processFulltextDocument",
  params = list(),
  output_dir = NULL,
  output_format = "parsed",
  parallel = length(files) > 5L,
  n_workers = .checkrefr_env$max_workers,
  progress = TRUE,
  mode = NULL,
  model_type = .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type,
  on_error = "warn",
  user_agent = NULL
)

    Arguments

    files

    character. Vector of full paths to the files to process. All files must exist on disk. PDF files are expected for all services except "processCitationList" which expects .txt files (one citation per line).

    service

    character. Name of the GROBID service to use. Accepted values:

    • "processFulltextDocument" - full text extraction

    • "processHeaderDocument" - header metadata extraction (title, authors, abstract, affiliations...)

    • "processReferences" - bibliographic reference extraction

    • "processCitationList" - parsing of citations from text files (one raw citation per line)

    Default: "processFulltextDocument". See the full list of available services in the official GROBID documentation.

    params

    list. Additional parameters passed to the HTTP form of the GROBID API, applied identically to all files in the batch. Common examples:

    • consolidateHeader = 1 - metadata enrichment via Crossref

    • consolidateCitations = 1 - reference enrichment via Crossref

    • includeRawCitations = 1 - include raw citations in the response

    These parameters correspond to the options accepted by the GROBID endpoints. For an exhaustive list, see the official API documentation. By default the argument is an empty list: list().

    output_dir

    character or NULL. If provided, each XML result is saved in this folder under the name {file_name}.tei.xml. The folder is created automatically if it does not exist. In this case, the function returns a vector of saved paths (invisible). If NULL, results are returned directly in memory. Default: NULL.

    output_format

    character. Format of the results returned when output_dir = NULL:

    • "raw" - named list (names = basename(files)) of raw XML/TEI strings

    • "parsed" - combined tibble (via dplyr::bind_rows())

    Default: "parsed".

    parallel

    logical If TRUE, processes files in parallel via future::multisession (see details). If FALSE, sequential processing. Default: length(files) > 5L.

    n_workers

    integer Number of workers to use in parallel mode. Automatically capped at max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1). For remote mode, a low value is recommended to avoid overloading the server. Default: .checkrefr_env$max_workers i.e. 4.

    progress

    logical Display a progress bar (sequential mode only). Default: TRUE.

    mode

    character or NULL. Connection mode to the GROBID server: "docker" or "remote". If NULL, uses the mode currently registered in the package's internal environment ("docker" by default if not configured). Default: NULL. Note on internal configuration: to persistently modify the mode or other global variables (port, timeout, etc.) for your R session, use checkrefr_set_defaults().

    model_type

    character or NA. GROBID model variant to use for bibliographic citation extraction. Two values are possible:

    • "crf" - model based solely on a CRF (Conditional Random Field). Faster, but generally less accurate than the "full" model.

    • "full" - model combining CRF and a neural (deep learning) model. More accurate, but slower and more resource intensive.

    This parameter corresponds to the model.name / citation configuration in GROBID's YAML config file (see the official documentation for details HERE). If NA (default value), in docker mode the sensible default model is used, see the GROBID dockerHub documentation for details or use the function grobid_docker_list_versions(). In remote mode a crf model is used by default. Default: .checkrefr_env$grobid_model_type, i.e. NA.

    on_error

    character Behavior in case of an error on a file:

    • "warn" - issues a warning and continues with the following files (the failing file produces NA in the results)

    • "stop" - immediately stops processing

    Default: "warn".

    user_agent

    character or NULL. Custom User-Agent string to send with each HTTP request to the GROBID API. Default: NULL.

    Value

    • output_dir provided -> vector of saved paths (invisible(character))

    • output_format = "raw" -> named list (names = basename(files)) of XML strings, or NA_character_ for failing files

    • output_format = "parsed" -> combined tibble with a source_file column, or invisible(NULL) if no parsed result is available

    Details

    The availability of the GROBID server (Docker or remote) is checked only once before batch processing (see grobid_docker_start() and grobid_remote_connect()).

    In case of an error on a given file, the behavior depends on on_error:

    • "warn" (default) - the failing file produces NA_character_ in the results, a warning is issued, and processing of the following files continues normally.

    • "stop" - processing stops immediately upon the first error encountered.

    When parallel = TRUE and n_workers > 1, processing is distributed via future::multisession (package future.apply). The sequential plan is automatically restored at the end of execution, even in case of error. The effective number of workers is capped at parallel::detectCores() - 1, i.e. the number of processor cores minus 1, regardless of the n_workers value provided, in order to preserve at least one core for the system.

    The params parameter is applied identically to all files in the batch; it is not possible to specify different parameters per file within a single call.

    References

    Official GROBID API documentation: https://grobid.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Grobid-service/

    See also

    grobid_process_file(), grobid_docker_start(), grobid_remote_connect(), parse_fulltext(), parse_header(), parse_references(), parse_citation_list(), checkrefr_set_defaults()

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example of a batch workflow using the package's example files

# 1. Retrieve example PDFs provided with the package
pdf_files <- system.file("extdata", package = "CheckrefR") |>
  list.files(pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE)

# 2. Start the GROBID server (Docker mode)
grobid_docker_start()

# 3. Sequential processing with progress bar, parsed result
fulltext_df <- grobid_process_files(
  files         = pdf_files,
  service       = "processFulltextDocument",
  output_format = "parsed"
)

# 4. Parallel processing with saving to disk
grobid_process_files(
  files      = pdf_files,
  service    = "processReferences",
  output_dir = tempdir(),
  parallel   = TRUE,
  n_workers  = 2L
)

# 5. Cleanly stop the Docker container
grobid_docker_stop()
} # }
